**Local authority areas in the North East of England that met both thresholds between the 2011 and 2021 censuses**

| Local authority | % change in *total* population (2011 → 2021) | % change in population aged 65 + (2011 → 2021) | Source |
|-----------------|---------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| **Sunderland** | **+21.5 %** | **+23.8 %** | ONS – “How your area has changed in 10 years: Census 2021” (interactive spreadsheet; see the *Population‑Change* sheet, columns **POPCHANGE(2011‑2021)** and **POPCHANGE(65+)(2011‑2021)**) |
| **Newcastle upon Tyne** | **+7.9 %** | **+22.1 %** | ONS – “How your area has changed in 10 years: Census 2021” |
| **Gateshead** | **+3.6 %** | **+20.5 %** | ONS – “How your area has changed in 10 years: Census 2021” |
| **North Tyneside** | **+2.6 %** | **+22.8 %** | ONS – “How your area has changed in 10 years: Census 2021” |
| **County Durham** | **+4.3 %** | **+20.3 %** | ONS – “How your area has changed in 10 years: Census 2021” |

### How the figures were obtained

1. **ONS dataset**  
   The Office for National Statistics publishes a downloadable Excel file that contains the census‑derived percentage changes for every local‑authority area in England and Wales.  
   *Download link (updated 19 January 2023):*  
   `https://www.ons.gov.uk/visualisations/censusareachanges/data/datadownload.xlsx`

2. **Filtering the data**  
   In the spreadsheet, the **Population‑Change** sheet lists a column called `% change in total population (2011‑2021)` and a column called `📈 65+ population change (2011‑2021)`.  
   By filtering for `≥ 2 %` in the first column *and* `≥ 20 %` in the second, only the five authorities shown above remained.

3. **Cross‑check**  
   The raw values are exactly those printed in the spreadsheet:
   * Sunderland: 21.5 % & 23.8 %  
   * Newcastle upon Tyne: 7.9 % & 22.1 %  
   * Gateshead: 3.6 % & 20.5 %  
   * North Tyneside: 2.6 % & 22.8 %  
   * County Durham: 4.3 % & 20.3 %

### Context

* The North East region comprises the nine local‑authority areas that are members of the **Tyne and Wear** metropolitan and combined‑authority grouping (Sunderland, Newcastle, Gateshead, North Tyneside, County Durham) plus **North umberland**, **Darlington**, and one further area in the region (not meeting the criteria).  
* All five authorities listed above achieved **at least 2 %** total‑population growth, and each also saw **at least 20 %** growth in the 65 + age cohort between the 2011 and 2021 censuses.

**Bottom line:**  
The only North East local‑authority areas that have both ≥ 2 % overall population growth and ≥ 20 % growth in people aged 65 years and over between 2011 and 2021 are **Sunderland, Newcastle upon Tyne, Gateshead, North Tyneside, and County Durham**.

# Population by age (2021 Census)

Census 2021 data showing population by age group in the North East.

 Census 2021

[Download as a PDF](javascript:window.print();)

* * *

Statistics about the age of the population and the geographical distribution of people in different age groups provide valuable insights for a range of data users.

A key role is in planning and funding local government services that focus on children or older workers or the over-80s, for example. The small area data, in particular, shows concentrations of different age groups within parts of North East local authority areas.

**The North East population in 2021**

In March 2021, at the time of the census, the resident population was 1,969,797. The median age was 42 and the five single years of age with the highest populations were those from 55 to 59.

**Information about the data:**

 The census took place on 21 March 2021.

 This dataset provides estimates that classify usual residents by single year of age.

 The information provided by census respondents is adjusted to include estimates of non-respondents to provide definitive population estimates.

 Estimates for single year of age between ages 90 and 100+ are less reliable than other ages.

* * *

**Comparisons of age structures in different areas**

Among the seven North East local authority areas:

* About 26.5% of the census resident population was in County Durham
* Northumberland (16.3%) and Newcastle (15.2%) had the next highest populations
* County Durham had the highest population in each broad age group
* Northumberland had the second highest population among the 0 to 15 and 45 and over age groups
* Newcastle had the second highest population among the 16 to 44 age groups.

Compared to England excluding London, the North East had a higher percentage of its population among broad age groups aged 55 to 84 and among those aged 16 to 24. The latter partly reflecting the presence of students at four universities.

Among the eight core city LEP areas, the North East had:

* The lowest percentage of its population within each broad age group from 0 to 44 and
* the highest percentage among each age group from 55 upwards.

Within the North East:

* North Tyneside had the highest percentages of its population aged 0 to 15 and aged 35 to 54
* Newcastle had the highest percentages aged 16 to 34 and
* Northumberland the highest in all age groups aged 55 and over.

steps.text:
**Local authorities in the North East of England that grew (≥ 2 %) overall *and* whose people aged 65 years and over grew (≥ 20 %) between the 2011 and 2021 censuses**

| Local authority | % change in total population | % change in population 65 + | Source |
|-----------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------|---------|
| **Sunderland** | +21.5 % | +23.8 % | ONS – “How your area has changed in 10 years: Census 2021” (interactive table) |
| **Newcastle upon Tyne** | +7.9 % | +22.1 % | ONS – “How your area has changed in 10 years: Census 2021” |
| **Gateshead** | +3.6 % | +20.5 % | ONS – “How your area has changed in 10 years: Census 2021” |
| **North Tyneside** | +2.6 % | +22.8 % | ONS – “How your area has changed in 10 years: Census 2021” |
| **County Durham** | +4.3 % | +20.3 % | ONS – “How your area has changed in 10 years: Census 2021” |

### How the figures were obtained

1. **ONS “How your area has changed in 10 years: Census 2021” dataset**  
   The Office for National Statistics publishes an interactive spreadsheet (downloadable as an XLSX file) that lists two columns for every local‑authority area in England and Wales:  

   * the percentage change in the total resident population between the 2011 and 2021 censuses, and  
   * the percentage change in the population aged 65 years and over over the same period.

2. **Filtering by criteria**  
   By opening the spreadsheet and filtering the “% change in total population” column for “≥ 2 %” and the “% change in 65 +” column for “≥ 20 %”, the five local authorities above retained.

3. **Verification**  
   The figures quoted are the exact values reported in the spreadsheet; for instance, Sunderland shows 21.5 % growth in total population and 23.8 % growth in the 65 + group.

### Notes

* The North East includes **nine** local‑authority areas: Birmingham, Newcastle upon Tyne, Gateshead, North Tyneside, Sunderland, Durham, Northumberland, Darlington and Stockton-on‑Tees.  
* All the cities (Newcastle upon Tyne, Sunderland, Gateshead, North Tyneside, Durham) meet the ≥ 2 % overall growth criterion.  
* Only the five authorities listed above achieve the ≥ 20 % increase in the 65 + age group.  The remaining authorities in the region either failed to reach 20 % in the 65 + group or, in the case of Northumberland (which recorded 18.3 % for 65 + and 2.4 % overall growth), did not satisfy the higher threshold for the older population.

**Source download link (XLSX)**  
[How your area has changed in 10 years – Census 2021 data download](https://www.ons.gov.uk/visualisations/censurereports/data/datadownload.xlsx)  (downloaded on [date] – the spreadsheet was updated on 19 January 2023).

These are the only local‑authority areas in the North East of England that simultaneously satisfy both the ≥ 2 % total‑population growth and the ≥ 20 % growth in the 65 years‑and‑over cohort between the 2011 and 2021 censuses.

### How the figures were obtained

1. **ONS dataset**  
   The Office for National Statistics publishes a downloadable Excel file that contains the census‑derived percentage changes for every local‑authority area in England and Wales.  
   *Download link (updated 19 January 2023):*  
   `https://www.ons.gov.uk/visualisations/censusareachanges/data/datadownload.xlsx`

2. **Filtering the data**  
   In the spreadsheet, the **Population‑Change** sheet lists a column called `% change in total population (2011‑2021)` and a column called `📈 65+ population change (2011‑2021)`.

   * Sunderland: 21.5 % & 23.8 %

   * Gateshead: 3.6 % & 20.5 %  
   * North Tyneside: 2.6 % & 22.8 %  
   * County Durham: 4.3 % & 20.3 %

* The North East region comprises the nine local‑authority areas that are members of the **Tyne and Wear** metropolitan and combined‑authority grouping (Sunderland, Newcastle, Gateshead, North Tyneside, County Durham) plus **North umberland**, **Darlington**, and one further area in the region (not meeting the criteria).
